description: workflow/04c_null_forest.smk: why is the importance of a random forest positive on average when the response is independent of the features (experiment B6)? A small simulation: same data and folds for every setting, one factor changed at a time from the baseline. Nothing is asserted about the sign or size of a forest importance; every row of the summary is 'reported'. Reading: docs/null_forest_investigation.md.

null_p5.note: p = 5 as in B6: floor(sqrt(q)) is 2 for the Full (q = 5) and for the Reduced model (q = 4)

null_p4.note: floor(sqrt(q)) is 2 for the Full (q = 4) and 1 for the Reduced model (q = 3)

null_p5_n1200.note: four times the rows: size of the effect and of the evaluation noise with more data

model: features: p-variate normal, unit variances, all correlations feature_correlation; y ~ N(0, 1) independent of the features; z ~ N(0, 1) independent of everything (an extra column, used by the variants padded_reduced and placebo_full only)
metric: mean squared error on the assessment rows; importance = MSE(Reduced) - MSE(Full), per split and anchor
seeding: forest for data set d, fold f, anchor index a (1-based), model m (0 Full, 1 Reduced): seed 100000 d + 1000 f + 10 a + m, the same in every variant and in both languages (the random number generators differ)

baseline.note: the forests of experiment B6: R = settings of the built-in "rand_forest" learner (ranger called directly), Python = python/sharedimp_exp/learners.py

mtry_as_full.note: both models draw floor(sqrt(p)) candidates, the number of the Full model

mtry_all.note: every column is a candidate at every split (bagging)

large_nodes.note: each language's own node-size parameter raised from 5 to 50

no_bootstrap.note: every tree sees every training row once; trees differ by the candidate draws only

padded_reduced.note: the Reduced model also gets the independent noise column z: both models have p columns

placebo_full.note: the Full model is the Reduced representation plus the noise column z (the anchor itself is not used): the 'importance' of pure noise

split6.note: the scikit-learn setting closest to the R built-in (docs/random_forest_comparison.md)

ols.note: ordinary least squares: the Full model estimates one coefficient more
